newsitem.title: ITALY: OLYMPICS-FIRST IOC VISITOR APPLAUDS ROME 2004 BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-FIRST IOC VISITOR APPLAUDS ROME 2004 BID.

text.p: The first member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to visit Rome since its bid for the 2004 Summer Games made a shortlist of five candidates praised what he had seen on Friday.
International Archery Federation president James Easton, an American, said the bid committee had impressed with their "preparedness" and had answered all his questions.

"They are almost acting like an organising committee in the plans and procedures they are putting in place," Easton told a news conference at the end if his stay in the capital, which joins Athens as a favourite to win the Games.
The other candidates are Cape Town, Buenos Aires and Stockholm. The final decision will be made on September 5 after IOC members have had a chance to visit the cities.
"From what I have seen, I think Rome has answered all the questions that I had and asked," said Easton.
"I certainly think Rome has remained in its role as one of the top two or three cities in my mind."
Easton said that after the Atlanta Games last summer, when transport proved a nightmare for many spectators and athletes, he had particularly wanted to see Rome's plans.

"Transport seems well organised at this early stage," he said. "I think the plans Rome has for traffic are really quite good...They are thinking about all the possible problems that could happen and have good answers for them."
Rome organised the 1990 World Cup, as well as hosting the 1960 Summer Olympics, and intends to use mostly existing venues for the 2004 Games if it wins the IOC's approval.
Easton applauded that decision and said he was also delighted with the proposed archery facilities.
Archery's future as an Olympic sport was in some doubt at the start of the decade but Easton said the 1992 Barcelona Games and Atlanta had given it a new lease of life.

In Atlanta, mini-television cameras were embedded in the bulls-eye and the sport attracted sell-out crowds who were encouraged to cheer and celebrate. Loud rock music was also broadcast between rounds.
"We have changed the look of archery," said Easton. "I think the IOC is much more happy with our sport and I believe we will remain in the Games schedule for the foreseeable future."
